===== FILE 3677__1.pdf =====
VIA Federal eRulemaking Portal 
 
August 18, 2025 
 
Secretary Douglas A. Collins 
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs 
810 Vermont Avenue NW 
Washington, DC 20420 
 
RE: Comments on Proposed Rule: Reproductive Health Services, 38 CFR Part 17 (August 4, 
2025), RIN 2900-AS31, Docket ID VA-2025-VHA-0073 
 
Dear Secretary Collins, 
 
On August 4, 2025, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) issued a Notice of Proposed 
Rulemaking (NPRM) to rescind Biden-era regulations that violate federal and state law. The 
NPRM would “return VA’s medical package and CHAMPVA benefits to where they were on 
September 8, 2022” which is prior to the Biden administration’s issuance of an interim final rule 
(IFR) that illegally expanded abortion on demand through the VA and asserted improper 
discretion for the VA Secretary to circumvent longstanding federal statute.1 Susan B. Anthony 
Pro-Life America strongly supports VA’s NPRM and asks that it be swiftly finalized and 
implemented.  
 
The plain reading of the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992 (VHCA) makes clear that the VA is 
statutorily prohibited from covering and counseling for abortion.2 For years prior to the Biden 
administration’s 2022 IFR, the VA medical benefits package and the Civilian Health and Medical 
Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA) excluded coverage and counseling 
for abortion—a fact that had been undisputed and uncontroversial for decades. The Biden 
administration’s IFR blatantly violated federal and state law by expanding coverage and 
counseling for abortion at the VA across the country. Though there are limited instances in which 
a state’s laws may be preempted by the VA, there is no instance in which a state’s laws may be 
 
1 Reproductive Health Services, 38 CFR Part 17, RIN 2900-AS31 (August 4, 2025), 
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-08-04/pdf/2025-14687.pdf 
2 Public Law 102-585 (1992, November 4), https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-106/pdf/STATUTE-
106-Pg4943.pdf#page=5 

preempted by the VA asserting a regulation that breaks federal law. The NPRM rightly reinstates 
the full exclusion of abortion and abortion counseling from the medical benefits package and 
CHAMPVA in accordance with federal statute. 
 
Additionally, the Biden administration’s IFR gave unnecessary and illegal discretion to the VA 
Secretary to expand abortion at the VA following the Dobbs decision in 2022. At the time 
Secretary McDonough claimed he had discretion to change abortion policy post-Dobbs,3 but this 
was not the case. This is not a matter of discretion but rather a matter of law. Because of the 
VHCA and the Deborah Samson Act of 2020, the VA Secretary is not allowed discretion to 
expand abortion beyond the limitations within the underlying statute. Further, in the time since 
the Biden administration’s IFR was issued, the Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) 
issued a decision in Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo.4 In this decision, SCOTUS held that 
statutory ambiguity does not indicate that Congress intended to give law-interpreting authority to 
an agency. Even if the VHCA and the Deborah Sampson Act of 2020 were ambiguous – which 
they are not – the VA is not entitled to deference for interpreting the law. Instead, VA is bound by 
the plain reading of the text – which is that the VA is statutorily prohibited from covering and 
counseling for abortion. By returning the VA’s medical package and CHAMPVA benefits to 
where they were on September 8, 2022, the NPRM not only follows the law, but it follows 
SCOTUS precedent that the VA does not have unfettered discretion to override congressional 
intent and duly enacted statute.    
 
The Biden administration sought to expand abortion in every facet of government and the VA 
was no exception. Under the Biden IFR policy, training documents,5 videos and slides obtained 
from the VA revealed disturbing and manipulative language that dehumanized the unborn and 
promoted abortion as the safest option for pregnant veterans.6 The NPRM under consideration 
brings back the rule of law to the VA by rescinding the Biden administration’s illegal IFR and 
reinstating the longstanding full exclusion on abortion and abortion counseling from the VA. 
Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America strongly supports this NPRM action and asks that it be 
swiftly finalized and implemented.
